title: Hephaestus — Variants across tellings
summary: Hephaestus, the lame smith god, forges divine weapons in his volcanic workshop. This study compares how different sources tell the tale.
body:
Hephaestus, the lame smith god, forges divine weapons in his volcanic workshop. He crafted Achilles's armor and Pandora's form.

No myth has one true version. Hephaestus survives in competing tellings — poets, priests, and painters each shaping it to their purpose. The variants disagree, and the disagreements are themselves revealing. Viewed through a contemporary-relevance lens, Hephaestus is brought into the present, where its patterns still appear in new clothes.

The 'real' Hephaestus is the whole cloud of versions, not any single text. A fifth sub-question considers how children first meet Hephaestus, and what the simplified versions leave out. Related entries in this archive: Oni and Gilgamesh.
